Wild realization this week.

For years I fought to get back a serious amount of money I had overpaid to the German tax office. Tax advisors, lawyers, an entire chain of middlemen that already cost me five figures over a few years.

Nothing ever moved. Every case just sat there, stalled, and nobody could even give me a compelling reason why.

Last week I decided to take it into my own hands. Called the tax office myself to understand what they actually needed to see, gathered every document I had, and ran the whole thing with Claude.

It took 5 days and a $100 max subscription.

Every single case was resolved yesterday in my favor. The money is already back in my account.

Here's the part nobody wants to say out loud: it was never the complexity, nor was it the evil government or tax office everyone loves to blame.

It was the middlemen. Slow, disorganized, constantly forgetting things, always taking the path of least resistance because your file is just one of 300 on their desk.

This week I realized how badly this entire profession is going to get wiped out. And you won't even be able to blame AI for it.

Blame the fact that almost nobody in it was doing the job properly in the first place.

You can think whatever you want about PumpFun, but this is exactly how you launch a token, and in my opinion a lot of teams could learn a thing or two from it.

One of the biggest issues in this industry is that most businesses launch their token way too early for quick liquidity, while the underlying fundamentals, aka actual cashflows, are nowhere near ready to support the price and absorb the sell pressure from early investors and their token overhang.

This is why most tokens just enter a perpetual downward spiral to zero. And since price drives narrative, the business itself starts suffering from it too, which then reflexively pushes the price down even further.

Tokens like $PUMP are one of the rare examples where the founders didn't rush the launch. They waited until revenues were already in the hundreds of millions.

I get that many prefer tokens because they give you early liquidity compared to equity or waiting for an IPO, which can often take way too long.

The real art is finding the right balance between both worlds.

You can think whatever you want about PumpFun, but this is exactly how you launch a token, and in my opinion a lot of teams could learn a thing or two from it.

One of the biggest issues in this industry is that most businesses launch their token way too early for quick liquidity, while the underlying fundamentals, aka actual cashflows, are nowhere near ready to support the price and absorb the sell pressure from early investors and their token overhang.

This is why most tokens just enter a perpetual downward spiral to zero. And since price drives narrative, the business itself starts suffering from it too, which then reflexively pushes the price down even further.

Tokens like $PUMP are one of the rare examples where the founders didn't rush the launch. They waited until revenues were already in the hundreds of millions.

I get that many prefer tokens because they give you early liquidity compared to equity or waiting for an IPO, which can often take way too long.

The real art is finding the right balance between both worlds.

Most crypto yield products launch a token and then go hunting for a business to justify it.

The Origin Vault from Axis is worth understanding because the product itself is a bit different from the usual stablecoin farm.

The easiest way to think about this vault is this:

The same dollar can trade at slightly different prices across different markets.

Axis tries to buy where it’s cheaper, sell where it’s higher, and repeat that across exchanges, assets, and settlement rails without taking a big directional bet on the market.

They’ve been doing that for eight years, with a reported 36% annualised return, 4.9 Sharpe, and $400M peak AUM.

The part that interested me is that they’re now putting the same engine onchain.

The Origin Vault takes USDT or USDC and, once the deposit window closes, puts the position into USDx and staked sUSDx for 30 days.

The target is 10 - 15% APY, with returns coming from the trading activity rather than a token emissions programme. Early deposits also earn 20 Coordinates per dollar per day.

There are obvious trade-offs. Funds are locked for 30 days, the return moves with strategy performance, and there’s more risk here than simply lending stables onchain.

Still, I think the model itself is worth watching.

A lot of crypto yield starts with a token and then looks for a reason to exist.

Axis is doing the opposite by taking an old trading business and turning access to it into an onchain product.

Pleased to partner with @AxisFDN on this one.
